<p class="language-switch"><a href="../">Version française ↗</a></p>

<div class="calendar-intro">

A measurement is not reality. A large sample is not necessarily representative. An average does not tell the whole story. And a model with a high score may not have learned what we think it has.

From **December 1 to 24, 2026**, this edition brings together twenty-four short investigations built around scientific questions worth examining. Each one starts from a paradox, an experiment, a surprising result or a difficult decision, then develops a clear explanation and, where useful, an experiment or visualization.

</div>

::: {.callout-note}
**How to use this edition.** This is not a 24-lesson course and it has no required reading order. Each investigation stands on its own: choose a question that interests you, move between topics, and return whenever you like. Links between days suggest connections, not prerequisites. **The five published articles are currently available in French**; the other links lead to public editorial outlines in French, not finished articles.
:::

## Six thematic entry points

The investigations are not divided into chronological blocks. A day can illuminate several questions, so the connections below form an **overlapping network of themes**, not six separate courses or a required sequence. Select a number to jump to its calendar door.

## Reading approach

Each investigation is self-contained and introduces the definitions and tools needed to follow it. Thematic links suggest comparisons and further questions, not prerequisites. Choose a day out of curiosity, or use the six topic areas to find a subject.

## About this edition

This 2026 edition is an independent editorial collection about data science, statistics and artificial intelligence. Published articles can be read directly; the remaining doors link to working outlines so that the editorial process is visible without presenting unfinished material as complete.
